```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_run-command.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Run an ARBITRARY command in the focused pane's cwd, inside a floating popup that
6	# closes by itself when the command exits. This is the generalisation of the
7	# hardcoded `prefix+G` (lazygit) binding — the tmux `display-popup -E` experience,
8	# with a command you pick or type instead of one baked into the config.
9	#
10	# Why a popup and not the alternatives:
11	#   - `type = "pane"` (prefix+G/M/N/`) splits the TILED layout for the duration.
12	#   - `prefix+c` + type + `exit` is four steps and churns the tab bar.
13	#   - `type = "popup"` (herdr >= 0.7.4) is session-modal and floats ABOVE the
14	#     layout, so nothing reflows and you land exactly where you were.
15	# It also cannot live as a herdr-plus Quick Action (prefix+y): those run through
16	# `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin — the same reason btop/nvtop are command panes — and
17	# every Quick Action is a fixed command string with no free-text field.
18	#
19	# Bound to prefix+E in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
20	#
21	# Usage:
22	#   run-command.sh [--cwd DIR] [--sh] [--] [QUERY...]
23	# --cwd  directory to run in; defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD (injected by the
24	#        keybind) → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd → $PWD. Preferring the env var
25	#        means this keeps working even when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a
26	#        stale server.
27	# --sh   run via `sh -c` (fast, no aliases) instead of the default `$SHELL -ic`
28	#        (sources the interactive rc, so this repo's aliases/functions resolve).
29	# QUERY  seeds the picker (and, with no fzf, prefills nothing — it is run as-is).
30	#
31	# Exit behaviour is governed by HERDR_RUN_HOLD:
32	#   fail (default)  close on success, wait for a key on non-zero exit
33	#   always          always wait for a key
34	#   never           never wait
35	#
36	# Consumers: the prefix+E keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
37	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Run any command in a popup".
38	set -eu
39	
40	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [--cwd DIR] [--sh] [--] [QUERY...]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
41	
42	cwd=""
43	use_sh=0
44	query=""
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
49	        --sh) use_sh=1; shift ;;
50	        -h|--help) usage ;;
51	        --) shift; break ;;
52	        -*) usage ;;
53	        *) break ;;
54	    esac
55	done
56	# Everything left (before or after `--`) seeds the query.
57	if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
58	    query="$*"
59	fi
60	
61	# --- cwd resolution: --cwd → $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD → pane foreground_cwd → $PWD
62	# (same chain as the sibling path-pick.sh).
63	if [ -z "$cwd" ]; then
64	    cwd="${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD:-}"
65	fi
66	if [ -z "$cwd" ] && command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
67	    pane="${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-}"
68	    if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	        pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
70	    fi
71	    if [ -n "$pane" ]; then
72	        cwd=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
73	            | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // .result.pane.cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
74	    fi
75	fi
76	[ -n "$cwd" ] && [ -d "$cwd" ] || cwd="$PWD"
77	
78	# --- history source ---------------------------------------------------------
79	# $HISTFILE is a zsh interactive var and is NOT exported into the `sh -c` context
80	# a keybind command runs in, so default it explicitly.
81	histfile="${HISTFILE:-$HOME/.zsh_history}"
82	
83	# Newest-first, de-duplicated, timestamps stripped.
84	#   - LC_ALL=C is REQUIRED: ~/.zsh_history carries non-UTF8 bytes and BSD sed
85	#     aborts with "sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence" under a UTF-8 locale.
86	#   - The reverse is done in awk because `tail -r` is BSD-only and `tac` GNU-only.
87	#   - Lines ending in a backslash are multi-line history entries; skip them.
88	_history() {
89	    [ -r "$histfile" ] || return 0
90	    LC_ALL=C sed 's/^: [0-9]*:[0-9]*;//' "$histfile" 2>/dev/null \
91	        | grep -v '\\$' \
92	        | awk 'NF' \
93	        | awk '{a[NR]=$0} END{for(i=NR;i>0;i--) if(!seen[a[i]]++) print a[i]}'
94	}
95	
96	# --- pick the command -------------------------------------------------------
97	cmd=""
98	if command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
99	    # --print-query + --expect together make the outcomes distinguishable.
100	    # Line layout is NOT fixed — fzf omits trailing lines it has nothing for:
101	    #
102	    #   Enter     with a match     rc 0    query \n ""        \n selection
103	    #   Alt+Enter with a match     rc 0    query \n alt-enter \n selection
104	    #   Enter     with no match    rc 1    query                              (1 line)
105	    #   Alt+Enter with no match    rc 1    query \n alt-enter
106	    #   Esc                        rc 130  —
107	    #
108	    # So the key is read from line 2 (empty/absent ⇒ plain Enter) and the
109	    # command from line 3 only on rc 0; every other path falls back to the
110	    # query on line 1. Verified against fzf directly with -1/-0.
111	    #
112	    # Alt+Enter exists because plain Enter cannot express "run exactly what I
113	    # typed" while fzf still has a match: if you type `ls -la` and history holds
114	    # `ls -la /tmp`, Enter takes the history entry. That made the picker feel
115	    # like it could only replay old commands. Alt+ (not Ctrl+) per the repo's
116	    # keybinding convention.
117	    set +e
118	    out=$(_history | fzf \
119	        --print-query --expect=alt-enter --no-sort --height=100% --border \
120	        --query="$query" \
121	        --header='enter: run highlighted · alt-enter: run what you typed · esc: cancel' \
122	        --prompt="run [$(basename "$cwd")]> ")
123	    rc=$?
124	    set -e
125	    case "$rc" in
126	        0 | 1) ;;
127	        *) exit 0 ;;   # 130 = Esc, or fzf failed — run nothing
128	    esac
129	    key=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '2p')
130	    if [ "$key" = "alt-enter" ]; then
131	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p')      # literal query, always
132	    elif [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
133	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '3p')      # highlighted selection
134	    else
135	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p')      # no match → the query
136	    fi
137	else
138	    if [ -n "$query" ]; then
139	        cmd="$query"
140	    else
141	        printf 'run [%s]> ' "$(basename "$cwd")"
142	        IFS= read -r cmd || exit 0
143	    fi
144	fi
145	
146	[ -n "$cmd" ] || exit 0
147	
148	# --- run it -----------------------------------------------------------------
149	cd "$cwd" || { echo "run-command: cannot cd to $cwd" >&2; exit 1; }
150	
151	set +e
152	if [ "$use_sh" -eq 1 ]; then
153	    sh -c "$cmd"
154	else
155	    # -i so the interactive rc is sourced and this repo's aliases/functions exist.
156	    "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -ic "$cmd"
157	fi
158	rc=$?
159	set -e
160	
161	# --- hold policy ------------------------------------------------------------
162	hold="${HERDR_RUN_HOLD:-fail}"
163	case "$hold" in
164	    never) ;;
165	    always) _wait=1 ;;
166	    *) [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && _wait=1 ;;
167	esac
168	if [ "${_wait:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
169	    [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && printf '\n[exit %s] ' "$rc" || printf '\n[exit 0] '
170	    printf 'press Enter to close…'
171	    IFS= read -r _ || true
172	fi
173	
174	exit "$rc"
175
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Open a NEW TAB rooted at the WORKSPACE ("space") directory, NOT the focused
6	# pane's live cwd.
7	#
8	# Why this exists: on herdr >=0.7.x, `new_cwd = "follow"` makes a new tab inherit
9	# the FOCUSED pane's cwd — herdr issue #912 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912)
10	# changed `follow` so new tabs behave like pane splits, and the older "new tab
11	# opens at the workspace's initial dir" was treated as a bug and removed. There
12	# is NO new_cwd value for "workspace dir", so we compute it and pass it via
13	# `herdr tab create --cwd`. (herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field either —
14	# `herdr workspace get` has no cwd — so it must be derived.)
15	#
16	# "Space dir" = the workspace's ROOT tab's pane cwd, where the root tab is the
17	# lowest-numbered tab — the one whose live-cwd basename herdr uses as the
18	# workspace label. We prefer the live cwd (foreground_cwd, matches the label),
19	# falling back to the shell startup cwd.
20	#
21	# Bound to prefix+C (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). prefix+c and the mouse
22	# "+" button keep herdr's native follow-the-focused-pane behavior. Uses the
23	# keybind-context $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (falls back to ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID).
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   new-tab-at-space-root.sh [pane_id]   # pane_id defaults to the current pane
27	set -eu
28	
29	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
30	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
31	
32	pane="${1:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}"
33	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: no pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)" >&2; exit 64; }
34	
35	wid=$(herdr pane get "$pane" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // ""')
36	[ -n "$wid" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
37	
38	# Root tab = lowest tab number in the workspace (herdr labels the space after it).
39	root_tab=$(herdr tab list --workspace "$wid" | jq -r '.result.tabs | sort_by(.number) | .[0].tab_id // ""')
40	[ -n "$root_tab" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: no tabs in workspace $wid" >&2; exit 1; }
41	
42	# `herdr tab get` returns tab metadata only (no pane cwd), so read the root tab's
43	# pane cwd from the full pane list. Prefer live cwd so it matches the space label.
44	root=$(herdr pane list | jq -r --arg t "$root_tab" \
45	    '.result.panes | map(select(.tab_id==$t)) | .[0] // {} | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
46	[ -n "$root" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve root dir for $root_tab" >&2; exit 1; }
47	
48	exec herdr tab create --workspace "$wid" --cwd "$root" --focus
49
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
10	#            the socket path that selects a non-default session — there is NO

16	# pane id to target another. herdr's keybind context passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID
17	# and herdr-plus Quick Actions pass $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID — both are wired to call
18	# this, and both fall through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
19	#

21	# auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52. We resolve it by absolute
22	# path fallback because a herdr command-pane / quick-action pane may run us via
23	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   pane-copy.sh process [PANE_ID]
27	#   pane-copy.sh coord   [PANE_ID]
28	#   pane-copy.sh content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
29	#
30	# Consumers: the prefix+P/L/V/B keybinds (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and
31	# the copy-pane-* quick actions (dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/

33	set -eu
34	
35	usage() {
36	    printf 'usage: %s process|coord|content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2
37	    exit 64
38	}
39	
40	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
41	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
42	
43	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
44	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
45	    X_BIN=x
46	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
47	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
48	else
49	    echo "pane-copy: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
50	    exit 1
51	fi
52	
53	action="${1:-}"
54	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
55	shift
56	
57	pane=""
58	source="recent"
59	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
60	    case "$1" in
61	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
62	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
63	        -*) usage ;;
64	        *)
65	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
66	                pane="$1"
67	                shift
68	            else
69	                usage
70	            fi
71	            ;;
72	    esac
73	done
74	
75	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
76	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
77	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
78	fi
79	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
80	
81	copy() { printf '%s' "$1" | "$X_BIN" copy; }
82	
83	case "$action" in
84	    process)
85	        info=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
86	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read process info for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
87	        text=$(printf '%s' "$info" | jq -r '
88	            .result.process_info as $p
89	            | "pane \($p.pane_id)  (shell pid \($p.shell_pid))",
90	              ( $p.foreground_processes[]?
91	                | "  \(.cmdline)  [pid \(.pid), cwd \(.cwd)]" )
92	        ')
93	        [ -n "$text" ] || text="pane $pane  (no foreground processes)"
94	        copy "$text"

96	        ;;

98	        pj=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
99	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }

101	        tb=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.tab_id // empty')
102	        pn=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
103	
104	        ws_label=$(herdr workspace get "$ws" 2>/dev/null \
105	            | jq -r '.result.workspace.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
106	        tb_label=$(herdr tab get "$tb" 2>/dev/null \

116	        text=$(printf 'session=%s\nworkspace=%s%s\ntab=%s%s\npane=%s\n' \
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
6	# herdr's per-pane metadata TOKENS (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source review
7	# --token review=…`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
8	# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
9	# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
10	# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
11	#
12	# Why a metadata token and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
13	# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. A pane can
14	# carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking
15	# into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
16	# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
17	#
18	# herdr >= 0.7.4 ONLY. herdr 0.7.4 removed `--custom-status` / the flat
19	# `custom_status` field in favour of this namespaced token map (up to 32 tokens
20	# per pane, names matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$). The removal is NOT listed as a
21	# breaking change upstream — on an older herdr this script dies with
22	# `unknown --custom-status`. See pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md.
23	#
24	# Unlike `custom_status`, a token is NOT rendered by the sidebar automatically —
25	# it only shows where a row layout references it. `$review` is wired into
26	# `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml; drop the
27	# token name here and you must drop it there too.
28	#
29	# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
30	# surfaces `tokens`, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) lets the
31	# `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No sidecar file.
32	#
33	# Usage:
34	#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
35	#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
36	#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
37	#
38	# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
39	# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
40	# focus_clear action. Keep TOKEN in sync with the `.tokens.<name>` lookups in
41	# that channel (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml) and with the
42	# `$review` token in the sidebar row layout.
43	set -eu
44	
45	SOURCE_ID='review'
46	TOKEN='review'                 # metadata token name; the tv channel keys off its PRESENCE
47	DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'
48	
49	usage() {
50	    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
51	    exit 64
52	}
53	
54	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
55	
56	action="${1:-}"
57	pane="${2:-}"
58	status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"
59	
60	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
61	[ -n "$pane" ] || usage
62	
63	_set() {
64	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --token "$TOKEN=$status" >/dev/null
65	    echo "review flag set on $pane"
66	}
67	
68	_clear() {
69	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --clear-token "$TOKEN" >/dev/null
70	    echo "review flag cleared on $pane"
71	}
72	
73	case "$action" in
74	    set)   _set ;;
75	    clear) _clear ;;
76	    toggle)
77	        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
78	        # Presence of the token IS the flag — a cleared token is absent from the
79	        # map, so no substring match is needed (unlike the pre-0.7.4 single
80	        # `custom_status` string that every source shared).
81	        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
82	            | jq -r --arg t "$TOKEN" '.result.pane.tokens[$t] // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
83	        case "$current" in
84	            '') _set ;;
85	            *)  _clear ;;
86	        esac ;;
87	    *) usage ;;
88	esac
89
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#

6	# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
7	# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
8	# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), then opens each choice via
9	# the repo's cross-platform `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open).
10	#
11	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
12	# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. The
13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs
16	# us via `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
20	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (passed by the keybind), else the current
21	# focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope);
22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
23	#
24	# Consumers: the prefix+u keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
25	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a URL from the pane".
26	set -eu
27	
28	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
29	
30	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
31	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
32	
33	# Resolve the opener (`x open`) even without the interactive PATH.
34	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
35	    X_BIN=x
36	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
37	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
38	else
39	    echo "url-pick: opener 'x' not found" >&2
40	    exit 1
41	fi
42	
43	pane=""
44	source="visible"
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
49	        -h|--help) usage ;;
50	        -*) usage ;;
51	        *)
52	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
53	                pane="$1"
54	                shift
55	            else
56	                usage
57	            fi
58	            ;;
59	    esac
60	done
61	
62	case "$source" in
63	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
64	    *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
65	esac
66	
67	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
68	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
70	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
71	fi
72	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
73	
74	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
75	    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
76	
77	# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, POSIX-ized
78	# (plain vars instead of bash arrays; trailing `|| true` so a no-match grep,
79	# which exits 1, does not trip `set -e`).
80	urls=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]' || true)
81	wwws=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
82	ips=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
83	gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
84	gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
85	npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)
86	
87	items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
88	
89	if [ -z "$items" ]; then
90	    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
91	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
92	    exit 0
93	fi
94	
95	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
96	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
97	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
98	
99	printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
100	    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
101	done
102
```

```text
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy-a-file-path picker — the copy-path sibling of url-pick.sh (which OPENS
6	# URLs). Reads the focused pane, extracts path-like tokens (borrowing extrakto's
7	# path heuristics), and presents a TWO-TIER fzf list: paths that EXIST relative to
8	# the pane cwd on top (copied as their resolved ABSOLUTE path), unverified
9	# candidates (as-seen) below a separator. The choice is copied via `x copy`.
10	#
11	# The existence check is the noise-killer extrakto lacks: file paths have no
12	# scheme:// marker, so regex alone matches dates (2024/01/02), rates (10k/s) and
13	# fractions (1/2); validating against the pane's live cwd drops nearly all of it.

15	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
16	# script exits), bound to prefix+p in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. Mirrors
17	# the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the keybind var) with a
18	# `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read` for the text, `x copy` for the
19	# clipboard, and an absolute-path `x` fallback because a command pane runs us via
20	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
21	#
22	# Usage:
23	#   path-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]
24	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, else the current focused pane. --source
25	# defaults to visible; --source recent scans the full scrollback. --cwd is the
26	# directory relative paths are resolved against for the existence check; it
27	# defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd →
28	# process-info cwd → $PWD.
29	#
30	# Consumers: the prefix+p keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
31	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Copy a file path from the pane".
32	set -eu
33	
34	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
35	
36	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
37	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
38	
39	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
40	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41	    X_BIN=x
42	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
43	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
44	else
45	    echo "path-pick: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
46	    exit 1
47	fi
48	
49	pane=""
50	source="visible"
51	cwd=""
52	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
53	    case "$1" in
54	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
55	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
56	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
57	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
58	        -h|--help) usage ;;
59	        -*) usage ;;
60	        *)
61	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
62	                pane="$1"
63	                shift
64	            else
65	                usage
66	            fi
67	            ;;
68	    esac
69	done
70	
71	case "$source" in
72	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
73	    *) echo "path-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
74	esac
75	
76	# Resolve pane (keybind passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID; fall back to current).
77	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
78	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
79	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
80	fi
81	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "path-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
82

84	if [ -z "$cwd" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
85	    cwd=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
86	    [ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
87	        | jq -r '.result.process_info.foreground_processes[0].cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
88	fi
89	[ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd="$PWD"
90	
91	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
92	    || { echo "path-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
93	
94	# Path candidates (extrakto path heuristics, POSIX-ized): slash-bearing tokens
95	# (abs /…, home ~/…, rel ./ ../ a/b/c) + bare filename.ext. rstrip trailing
96	# ",):; then drop rate/fraction noise (extrakto's exclude: 10k/s, 1/2). dedupe.
97	cands=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" \
98	    | grep -oE '(~|\.\.?)?/?[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+)+|[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8}' \
99	    | sed -E 's/[",):;]+$//' \
100	    | grep -vE '^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$|[kKmMgG]/s$' \
101	    | grep -v '^$' | awk '!seen[$0]++' || true)
102	
103	if [ -z "$cands" ]; then
104	    printf 'path-pick: no file paths found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
105	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
106	    exit 0
107	fi
108	
109	# Two tiers: exists-under-cwd (resolved absolute) vs the rest (as-seen).
110	exist=""
111	maybe=""
112	OLDIFS=$IFS
113	IFS='
114	'
115	for c in $cands; do
116	    base=$(printf '%s' "$c" | sed -E 's/:[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$//')   # strip :line[:col] for the test
117	    case "$base" in
118	        /*)   abs="$base" ;;
119	        \~/*) abs="$HOME/${base#\~/}" ;;
120	        *)    abs="$cwd/$base" ;;
121	    esac
122	    if [ -e "$abs" ]; then
123	        rp=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$abs")" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s/%s' "$(pwd -P)" "$(basename -- "$abs")") \
124	            || rp="$abs"
125	        exist="$exist$rp
126	"
127	    else
128	        maybe="$maybe$c
129	"
130	    fi
131	done
132	IFS=$OLDIFS
133	
134	exist=$(printf '%s' "$exist" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
135	maybe=$(printf '%s' "$maybe" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
136	
137	SEP='────────  unverified (not found under cwd)  ────────'
138	list=$(
139	    [ -n "$exist" ] && printf '%s\n' "$exist"
140	    [ -n "$maybe" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$SEP"; printf '%s\n' "$maybe"; }
141	)
142	
143	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
144	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$list" | fzf --multi --no-sort --height=100% --border \
145	    --prompt='path> ' --header="Enter=copy · Tab=multi · cwd=$cwd") || exit 0
146	
147	# Drop the separator if it slipped into the selection; copy the rest.
148	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | grep -vFx "$SEP" | grep -v '^$' || true)
149	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
150	
151	printf '%s' "$chosen" | "$X_BIN" copy
152	echo "copied $(printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | grep -c .) path(s)"
153
```

```text
# Session/workspace switcher cable channel for herdr (tv) — sesh analog
#
# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches
# herdr WORKSPACES (the project-level unit) and opens new ones from zoxide
# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
#
# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.

[metadata]
name = "herdr-sesh"
description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]

[source]
command = [
  '''herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]? | "ws\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.label)  (\(.pane_count)p, \(.tab_count)t)"' ''',
  '''zoxide query -l 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{print "dir",$0,$0}' ''',
]
display = "{split:\t:2}"
output = "{split:\t:1}"

[preview]
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
case "$kind" in
  ws)
    printf '\033[1mworkspace %s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
    herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq . 2>/dev/null \
      || herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null
    ;;
  dir)
    printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
    if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then eza -la --git --color=always "$ref" 2>/dev/null
    else ls -la "$ref" 2>/dev/null; fi
    ;;
esac
'''

[ui]
input_header = "herdr Workspaces / Dirs"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open"
ctrl-d = ["actions:close_ws", "reload_source"]

[actions.open]
description = "Focus the workspace, or open a new workspace at the directory"
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0
case "$kind" in
  ws)  herdr workspace focus "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  dir) herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
esac
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.close_ws]
description = "Close the selected herdr workspace"
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
[ "$kind" = "ws" ] && [ -n "$ref" ] && herdr workspace close "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"
════════ dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml (     101 lines)
# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant
#
# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists
# panes from the running herdr server and lets you jump to the one running an
# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).
#
# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)

[metadata]
name = "herdr-agent-panes"
description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.agent_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'
printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  [%s]\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
'''

[ui]
input_header = "Live herdr Agent Panes"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:focus"
alt-t = "actions:focus"
alt-k = "actions:close_pane"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"

[actions.focus]
description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab"
command = '''
ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.close_pane]
description = "Close the pane (confirm prompt)"
command = '''
p='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$p" ] && exit 0
printf 'Close pane %s? [y/N] ' "$p"
read -r ans
case "$ans" in
  y|Y|yes|YES) herdr pane close "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "closed $p" || echo "failed (already gone?)" ;;
  *) echo "aborted" ;;
esac
echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _
'''
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy_id]
description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"
```

```text
=== mac herdr-review.toml ===
# Review-pending inbox cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware
#
# Lists herdr panes carrying a "review-pending" flag (⭐) — the ones whose agent
# finished but you haven't reviewed yet. Companion to `herdr-agent-panes.toml`;
# the flag is set by hmark / prefix+m (see dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh)
# and stored as the pane's `review` metadata TOKEN, orthogonal to agent state.
# Bound to `prefix+i` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB but KEEPS the ⭐ (you may still be
# mid-review). Alt+C = focus AND clear the flag ("mark read"). herdr has no
# "focus pane by id" (pane focus is directional only), so we focus at tab
# granularity — enough with one agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) via jq,
# filtered to panes that HAVE a non-empty `tokens.review` — presence is the flag,
# so the glyph text is free-form. Keep the token name in sync with TOKEN in
# review-mark.sh. herdr >= 0.7.4 (0.7.4 replaced the flat `custom_status` field
# with this token map; on older herdr the filter silently matches nothing):
#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
#   3. tokens.review  (⭐ REVIEW)
#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)

[metadata]
name = "herdr-review"
description = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐) — jump to sessions you flagged for later"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | select((.tokens.review? // "") != "") | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.tokens.review)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:3}  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'
printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
'''

[ui]
input_header = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐)"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:focus"
alt-t = "actions:focus"
alt-c = ["actions:focus_clear", "reload_source"]
ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"

[actions.focus]
description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab (keep the ⭐)"
command = '''
ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.focus_clear]
description = "Jump to the pane AND clear the ⭐ (mark read)"
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'; ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$pane" ] && "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh" clear "$pane" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_id]
description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_dir]
description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:4}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"

=== quick-actions dir listing ===

copy-pane-visible.toml
github.toml

open-repo.toml

--- sample: copy-pane-visible.toml ---

name = "Copy pane: content (visible)"
```

```toml
{{- $herdrDir := printf "%s/.config/herdr" (.chezmoi.homeDir | replace "\\" "/") -}}
# herdr — native Windows terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (preview beta).
#
# Windows port of the parent dotfiles repo's .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# It mirrors the tmux/unix keymap as closely as the Windows build allows; every
# binding that could NOT be carried over is listed in
# backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md with the reason.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves the keys herdr writes back at
# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state).
# Tracking this as a PLAIN managed file — which is what this repo did before —
# clobbers that writeback and can re-trigger onboarding.
#
# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
# Full default: `herdr --default-config`
# Validate after editing: `herdr server reload-config` (expect empty diagnostics)
#
# Helper-script paths are baked ABSOLUTE at render time on purpose: `pwsh -File`
# does NOT expand a leading `~` (verified), and herdr passes the command string
# through without shell tilde expansion on Windows.
#
# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux).

[update]
# Windows builds are preview-only; the installer rejects "stable" here.
# Re-asserted by the overlay as a single key so herdr's own [update] bookkeeping
# (last-check timestamps etc.) survives an apply.
channel = "preview"

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"           # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true

# "auto" draws herdr's own cursor on Windows to avoid ConPTY flicker;
# set "native" to hand the cursor to the outer terminal. Windows-only key.
host_cursor = "auto"

# Agent sidebar ordering. herdr's default is "spaces" (grouped by space);
# "priority" turns the panel into an attention queue (blocked/waiting agents
# float to the top). With many concurrent agent panes the queue is what you
# actually scan. Valid values: "spaces" | "priority".
agent_panel_sort = "priority"

# Expanded Agent sidebar row layout. herdr's own default is
#   [["state_icon", "workspace", "tab"], ["agent"]]
# and we append the `$review` metadata token so the review-pending ⭐
# (prefix+m / hmark) is actually VISIBLE in the sidebar.
#
# Required since herdr 0.7.4: `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field
# were replaced by a namespaced token map, and unlike custom_status a token is
# rendered ONLY where a row layout names it — set a token with no layout entry
# and the flag silently exists in the API but shows up nowhere.
#
# Keep `$review` in sync with $Token in dot_config/herdr/review-mark.ps1.
# NOTE this pins the layout: upstream changes to the default rows will NOT reach
# us, so re-check this block against `herdr --default-config` on herdr upgrades.
[ui.sidebar.agents]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "tab", "$review"],
  ["agent"],
]

[terminal]
# Match the rest of this repo (WezTerm / Windows Terminal default to pwsh).
default_shell = "pwsh"
# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd):
#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
# cwd — same as a split (herdr issue #912). NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at
# the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for that use the prefix+C command below.
new_cwd = "follow"

# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
# Only existing actions can be rebound; herdr defaults are kept for everything
# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings, so one action can
# carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
[keys]
split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup
new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit

# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; these add the workspace + agent
# analogs so a number key jumps directly. "N..M" is native herdr config syntax.
# On the unix side prefix+SHIFT+digit was found unusable (under the kitty
# keyboard protocol shift+1 still carries the printable "!"), hence ctrl/alt.
# Whether Windows/ConPTY behaves the same is UNVERIFIED — see the backlog note.
switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N
focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane

# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]

# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
# type = "pane": a temporary pane that closes when the command exits — herdr's
# analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused pane's
# cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.
# type = "popup" (herdr >= 0.7.4) floats ABOVE the tiled layout instead, so
# nothing reflows — used for the two bindings you stay inside for a while.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+G"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"

# btop as a floating command pane (a real PTY that closes when you quit it).
# Quick Actions can't host this: herdr-plus runs an action with no PTY/stdin, so
# an interactive TUI exits immediately.
# NOTE: the unix config also binds prefix+N to nvtop — deliberately NOT ported,
# nvtop is Linux-only. See backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+M"
type = "pane"
command = "btop"
description = "btop system monitor (popup pane)"

# --- Scratch shell as a real floating popup (prefix+`) ---
# type = "popup" floats above the layout, so quitting the shell puts you back
# exactly where you were. lazygit/btop above deliberately stay type = "pane":
# you quit those immediately and popups are session-modal.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+`"
type = "popup"
command = "pwsh"
width = "85%"
height = "80%"
description = "scratch shell (popup)"

# --- Run an arbitrary command in a floating popup (prefix+E) ---
# The generalisation of prefix+G: fzf-pick or type any command, run it in the
# FOCUSED PANE'S cwd, and the popup closes itself when the command exits.
# Enter runs the highlighted history entry; Alt+Enter runs exactly what you typed.
# Exit behaviour: closes on success, holds on failure. Override with
# $env:HERDR_RUN_HOLD = 'always'|'never'.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+E"
type = "popup"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/run-command.ps1"'
width = "80%"
height = "70%"
description = "run a command in the pane cwd (popup)"

# --- New tab at the workspace ("space") root dir (prefix+C) ---
# herdr's native new-tab (prefix+c) and the mouse "+" button follow new_cwd,
# which on herdr >=0.7.x means the FOCUSED pane's live cwd. This binding instead
# opens a new tab at the workspace ROOT dir — the lowest-numbered tab's pane cwd,
# i.e. what herdr uses for the space label. prefix+c keeps native behaviour.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+C"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/new-tab-at-space-root.ps1" "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID"'
description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"

# URL picker (tmux prefix+u analog — joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads the focused
# pane, fzf-picks a URL (same rewrites: http(s)/ftp/file, www., IP, git@ remote,
# quoted owner/repo, npm import), opens it with the Windows shell handler.
# Visible screen by default; `--source recent` scans full scrollback.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+u"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/url-pick.ps1" "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID"'
description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+T"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-sesh"
description = "Session / workspace / dir switcher (herdr-aware tv channel)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+a"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-agent-panes"
description = "Live agent panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"

# --- Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ---
# prefix+m toggles a per-pane "I still need to review this" flag (a herdr
# metadata token, orthogonal to agent state — it survives the pane going idle
# when you peek in). prefix+i opens the flagged-panes inbox.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+m"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/review-mark.ps1" toggle "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID"'
description = "toggle review-pending flag (⭐) on the current pane"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+i"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-review"
description = "Review-pending inbox — flagged panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"

# --- Copy focused-pane facts to the clipboard (prefix+P/D/V/S) ---
# One helper (pane-copy.ps1) distills a pane's data and pipes it to Set-Clipboard.
# The SAME four ops are also herdr-plus Quick Actions. Uppercase letters resolve
# to prefix+shift+<letter>; P/D/V/S avoid herdr's reserved shift builtins
# (shift+H/J/K/L swap-pane) and this repo's shift+B / shift+R.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+P"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/pane-copy.ps1" process "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID"'
description = "copy pane process info"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+D"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/pane-copy.ps1" coord "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID"'
description = "copy pane coordinate (session>space>tab>pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+V"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/pane-copy.ps1" content "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID" --source visible'
description = "copy pane content (visible screen)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+S"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/pane-copy.ps1" content "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID" --source recent'
description = "copy pane content (full scrollback)"

# Copy a file PATH from the pane (extrakto-style). Extracts path-like tokens;
# two-tier: paths that EXIST under the pane cwd (copied as resolved absolute) on
# top, unverified candidates below a separator. Lowercase p pairs with the
# uppercase copy family (P/D/V/S), same u/U convention as the unix side.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+p"
type = "pane"
command = 'pwsh -NoProfile -File "{{ $herdrDir }}/path-pick.ps1" "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID" --cwd "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD"'
description = "copy a file path from the pane (fzf, two-tier)"

# --- herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + popup-menu analog) ---
# Requires: herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus
# Projects = declarative multi-pane workspace templates; Quick Actions = fuzzy
# command launcher. If the plugin is not installed these bindings simply no-op.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+O"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects"
description = "herdr-plus: Projects (layout launcher)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+y"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions"
description = "herdr-plus: Quick Actions"

```

```tmpl
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Runs under pwsh via [interpreters.ps1] in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl. chezmoi pipes the
# CURRENT target file into stdin and takes the new contents from stdout.
#
# WHY AN OVERLAY (this replaced a plain managed dot_config/herdr/config.toml):
# herdr rewrites this file at runtime — the onboarding flag, in-app settings
# popups, [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state. A plain managed
# file clobbers all of that on every `chezmoi apply`, which can re-trigger
# onboarding. The parent (unix) repo hit this and moved create_ -> modify_ on
# 2026-07-06; this repo's config was added five days later and still used the
# plain form. Same fix, ported.
#
# MERGE MODEL — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
#   - Every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file that is NOT managed and NOT already in
#     the template is copied across (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
#     [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins).
#   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table
#     keeps herdr's own bookkeeping. Windows needs exactly one: update.channel
#     must stay "preview" (the installer rejects "stable" on Windows builds), but
#     [update] also holds herdr's last-check state, which we do not want to wipe.
#     This sub-key merge is the one deliberate divergence from the unix overlay.
#
# WHY tomlkit (not a hand-rolled emitter): herdr's config has an array-of-tables
# ([[keys.command]]) and comments worth keeping; stdlib tomllib is read-only.
# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees >=3.11 -> stdlib tomllib), fall back to
# system python, then to emitting the raw template (a fresh host with neither
# still gets a full config — note we emit the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a
# fresh host stdin is empty).
#
# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# Validate the result with `herdr server reload-config` (empty diagnostics).

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# Emit bytes verbatim so nothing re-encodes the config's ⭐ / box-drawing glyphs
# and no BOM or trailing CRLF churn creeps into chezmoi's diff.
function Write-StdoutBytes {
    param([byte[]] $Bytes)
    $out = [Console]::OpenStandardOutput()
    $out.Write($Bytes, 0, $Bytes.Length)
    $out.Flush()
}

$utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)   # no BOM

$templateText = @'
{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
'@

$liveText = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd()

$tmpDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
$stamp = [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName()
$tmplFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-tmpl-$stamp.toml"
$liveFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-live-$stamp.toml"
$pyFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-merge-$stamp.py"
$outFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-out-$stamp.toml"

try {
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($tmplFile, $templateText, $utf8)
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($liveFile, $liveText, $utf8)

    # Pick a Python. uv is in this repo's scoop package set; `python` is the
    # uv-managed default install (--default --preview creates the unversioned shim).
    $py = $null
    if (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('uv', 'run', '--no-project', '--quiet', '--with', 'tomlkit', '--python', '>=3.11', 'python')
    } elseif (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('python')
    } elseif (Get-Command python3 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('python3')
    }

    if (-not $py) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine('modify_config.toml: no uv/python found; emitting managed template (runtime keys not preserved this run)')
        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
        return
    }

    $pySource = @'
import os
import sys

tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]
out_path = os.environ["HERDR_OUT_FILE"]

with open(tmpl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    template_text = fh.read()


def emit(text):
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        fh.write(text)


try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader -> can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is.
        emit(template_text)
        sys.exit(0)

try:
    import tomlkit
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print(
        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    emit(template_text)
    sys.exit(0)

# Tables the template owns outright.
MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}

with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    live_text = fh.read().strip()

doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
try:
    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
    live = {}

for key, value in live.items():
    if key in MANAGED:
        continue
    if key in doc:
        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
        continue
    doc[key] = value

for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
    if table not in doc:
        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value

emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
'@

    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)

    $env:HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE = $tmplFile
    $env:HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
    $env:HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile

    $exe = $py[0]
    $rest = @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) + @($pyFile)
    & $exe @rest
    $rc = $LASTEXITCODE

    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
        return
    }

    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
} finally {
    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    foreach ($v in 'HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE', 'HERDR_LIVE_FILE', 'HERDR_OUT_FILE') {
        Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}
```

chezmoi execute-template --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --source="$PWD" < some.ps1.tmpl > r.ps1  # then parse r.ps1 with pwsh

```ps1
# ~/.config/herdr/_common.ps1
# Source: dot_config/herdr/_common.ps1 (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Shared helpers for the herdr keybind scripts (run-command / new-tab-at-space-root /
# url-pick / path-pick / pane-copy / review-mark). Dot-sourced by each of them.
#
# These run inside a herdr `[[keys.command]]` pane or popup, spawned as
# `pwsh -NoProfile -File <script> …` — so there is NO profile, NO repo aliases and
# NO $PROFILE-set encoding. Everything they need has to come from here or the
# environment herdr injects ($HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD /
# $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH).
#
# The unix originals shell out to `jq` and to this repo's cross-platform `x`
# helper (`x copy` / `x open`). Neither exists on Windows: JSON is parsed with
# ConvertFrom-Json, the clipboard is Set-Clipboard, and opening a URL is
# Start-Process (the Windows shell handler). `jq` IS installed here, but calling
# it would only add a process per lookup.

Set-StrictMode -Off
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# herdr emits UTF-8; without this a pane read full of box-drawing characters
# comes back mojibake under -NoProfile (the repo's UTF-8 console setup lives in
# the profile, which we deliberately skip).
try {
    [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
    $OutputEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
} catch { $null = $_ }

function Test-HerdrPresent {
    if (Get-Command herdr -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { return $true }
    Write-Host 'herdr not found on PATH' -ForegroundColor Red
    $false
}

# Run a herdr subcommand and parse its JSON. Returns $null on any failure so
# callers can fall through instead of throwing inside a pane that is about to close.
function Invoke-HerdrJson {
    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)
    try {
        $raw = & herdr @Argument 2>$null
        if (-not $raw) { return $null }
        return ($raw | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop)
    } catch { return $null }
}

# Resolve the pane to act on: explicit id -> $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (what a keybind
# injects) -> $HERDR_PANE_ID (ambient, set inside a pane) -> `herdr pane current`.
function Resolve-HerdrPane {
    param([string] $PaneId)
    foreach ($candidate in $PaneId, $env:HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, $env:HERDR_PANE_ID) {
        if ($candidate) { return $candidate }
    }
    $j = Invoke-HerdrJson pane current
    if ($j) { return $j.result.pane.pane_id }
    $null
}

# Resolve a working directory: explicit -> $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD (injected by the
# keybind) -> the pane's live foreground cwd -> the process cwd. Preferring the env
# var means this keeps working even when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a
# stale server.
function Resolve-HerdrCwd {
    param([string] $Cwd, [string] $PaneId)
    if ($Cwd -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Cwd)) { return $Cwd }
    if ($env:HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $env:HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD)) {
        return $env:HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD
    }
    if ($PaneId) {
        $j = Invoke-HerdrJson pane get $PaneId
        if ($j) {
            foreach ($c in $j.result.pane.foreground_cwd, $j.result.pane.cwd) {
                if ($c -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $c)) { return $c }
            }
        }
    }
    (Get-Location).Path
}

# Read a pane's terminal text. $Source is visible | recent | recent-unwrapped.
function Get-HerdrPaneText {
    param([string] $PaneId, [string] $Source = 'visible')
    try {
        $out = & herdr pane read $PaneId --source $Source --format text 2>$null
        if ($out -is [array]) { return ($out -join "`n") }
        return [string]$out
    } catch { return $null }
}

# Copy to the Windows clipboard. Set-Clipboard is the native equivalent of the
# unix side's `x copy`; clip.exe is the fallback for a host where the
# Microsoft.PowerShell.Management clipboard cmdlets are unavailable.
function Set-HerdrClipboard {
    param([string] $Text)
    try {
        Set-Clipboard -Value $Text -ErrorAction Stop
        return $true
    } catch {
        if (Get-Command clip.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
            $Text | clip.exe
            return $true
        }
        Write-Host "could not reach the clipboard: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
        return $false
    }
}

# A herdr command pane closes the moment this script exits, so an error the user
# never sees is an error that never happened. Hold briefly.
function Show-HerdrNotice {
    param([string] $Message, [double] $Seconds = 1.5)
    Write-Host $Message -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Start-Sleep -Seconds $Seconds
}

```

```ps1
# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.ps1
# Source: dot_config/herdr/review-mark.ps1 (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
# herdr's per-pane metadata TOKENS (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source review
# --token review=…`). PowerShell port of the parent repo's
# dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh.
#
# Why a metadata token and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. A pane can
# carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking
# into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
#
# herdr >= 0.7.4 ONLY. 0.7.4 removed `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status`
# field in favour of this namespaced token map. The removal is NOT listed as a
# breaking change upstream — on an older herdr this dies with
# `unknown --custom-status`.
#
# Unlike `custom_status`, a token is NOT rendered by the sidebar automatically —
# it only shows where a row layout references it. `$review` is wired into
# `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml; drop the
# token name here and you must drop it there too.
#
# Usage:
#   review-mark.ps1 set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
#   review-mark.ps1 clear  <pane_id>
#   review-mark.ps1 toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]
#
# Consumers: the prefix+m keybind, the herdr-review tv channel's focus_clear
# action, and hmark/hunmark in profile.d/25_herdr.ps1.

param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)

. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '_common.ps1')

$SourceId = 'review'
$Token = 'review'            # the tv channel keys off its PRESENCE, not its text
$DefaultStatus = "$([char]0x2B50) REVIEW"

function Show-Usage {
    Write-Host 'usage: review-mark.ps1 set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]'
    exit 64
}

if (-not (Test-HerdrPresent)) { exit 1 }

$action = if ($Argument.Count -ge 1) { $Argument[0] } else { '' }
$paneArg = if ($Argument.Count -ge 2) { $Argument[1] } else { '' }
$status = if ($Argument.Count -ge 3) { $Argument[2] } else { $DefaultStatus }

if (-not $action) { Show-Usage }

$pane = Resolve-HerdrPane -PaneId $paneArg
if (-not $pane) { Write-Host 'review-mark: could not determine a pane id' -ForegroundColor Red; exit 1 }

function Set-ReviewFlag {
    & herdr pane report-metadata $pane --source $SourceId --token "$Token=$status" | Out-Null
    Write-Host "review flag set on $pane"
}

function Clear-ReviewFlag {
    & herdr pane report-metadata $pane --source $SourceId --clear-token $Token | Out-Null
    Write-Host "review flag cleared on $pane"
}

switch ($action) {
    'set' { Set-ReviewFlag }
    'clear' { Clear-ReviewFlag }
    'toggle' {
        # Presence of the token IS the flag — a cleared token is absent from the
        # map, so no substring match is needed (unlike the pre-0.7.4 single
        # `custom_status` string that every source shared).
        $j = Invoke-HerdrJson pane get $pane
        $current = ''
        if ($j -and $j.result.pane.PSObject.Properties['tokens'] -and $j.result.pane.tokens) {
            $t = $j.result.pane.tokens
            if ($t.PSObject.Properties[$Token]) { $current = [string]$t.$Token }
        }
        if ($current) { Clear-ReviewFlag } else { Set-ReviewFlag }
    }
    default { Show-Usage }
}
```

```ps1
# ~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.ps1
# Source: dot_config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.ps1 (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Open a NEW TAB rooted at the WORKSPACE ("space") directory, NOT the focused
# pane's live cwd. PowerShell port of the parent repo's
# dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh.
#
# Why this exists: on herdr >=0.7.x, `new_cwd = "follow"` makes a new tab inherit
# the FOCUSED pane's cwd — herdr issue #912 changed `follow` so new tabs behave
# like pane splits, and the older "new tab opens at the workspace's initial dir"
# was treated as a bug and removed. There is NO new_cwd value for "workspace
# dir", so we compute it and pass it via `herdr tab create --cwd`. (herdr exposes
# no workspace-level cwd field either — `herdr workspace get` has no cwd — so it
# must be derived.)
#
# "Space dir" = the workspace's ROOT tab's pane cwd, where the root tab is the
# lowest-numbered tab — the one whose live-cwd basename herdr uses as the
# workspace label. We prefer the live cwd (foreground_cwd, matches the label),
# falling back to the shell startup cwd.
#
# Bound to prefix+C. prefix+c and the mouse "+" button keep herdr's native
# follow-the-focused-pane behaviour.
#
# Usage:
#   new-tab-at-space-root.ps1 [pane_id]

param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)

. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '_common.ps1')

if (-not (Test-HerdrPresent)) { exit 1 }

$paneArg = if ($Argument -and $Argument.Count -ge 1) { $Argument[0] } else { '' }
$pane = Resolve-HerdrPane -PaneId $paneArg
if (-not $pane) {
    Show-HerdrNotice 'new-tab-at-space-root: no pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)'
    exit 64
}

$paneJson = Invoke-HerdrJson pane get $pane
$wid = if ($paneJson) { $paneJson.result.pane.workspace_id } else { $null }
if (-not $wid) {
    Show-HerdrNotice "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $pane"
    exit 1
}

# Root tab = lowest tab number in the workspace (herdr labels the space after it).
$tabs = Invoke-HerdrJson tab list --workspace $wid
$rootTab = $null
if ($tabs -and $tabs.result.tabs) {
    $rootTab = ($tabs.result.tabs | Sort-Object { [int]$_.number } | Select-Object -First 1).tab_id
}
if (-not $rootTab) {
    Show-HerdrNotice "new-tab-at-space-root: no tabs in workspace $wid"
    exit 1
}

# `herdr tab get` returns tab metadata only (no pane cwd), so read the root tab's
# pane cwd from the full pane list. Prefer live cwd so it matches the space label.
$panes = Invoke-HerdrJson pane list
$root = $null
if ($panes -and $panes.result.panes) {
    $rootPane = $panes.result.panes | Where-Object { $_.tab_id -eq $rootTab } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($rootPane) {
        foreach ($c in $rootPane.foreground_cwd, $rootPane.cwd) { if ($c) { $root = $c; break } }
    }
}
if (-not $root) {
    Show-HerdrNotice "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve root dir for $rootTab"
    exit 1
}

& herdr tab create --workspace $wid --cwd $root --focus
exit $LASTEXITCODE

```

```ps1
# ~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.ps1
# Source: dot_config/herdr/pane-copy.ps1 (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Copy distilled facts about a herdr pane to the Windows clipboard. PowerShell
# port of the parent repo's dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh. Three targets:
#
#   process  the foreground processes running in the pane (cmdline + pid + cwd)
#   coord    the pane's coordinate in herdr's Session > Workspace > Tab > Pane
#            hierarchy, in a paste-ready form (the ids the herdr CLI accepts, plus
#            the socket path that selects a non-default session — there is NO
#            --session flag on the pane/tab/workspace subcommands)
#   content  the pane's terminal content — visible screen (--source visible) or
#            the full retained scrollback (--source recent, the default)
#
# The pane defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (injected by the keybind), then
# $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID's herdr-plus equivalent, then `herdr pane current`.
#
# Clipboard sink is Set-Clipboard — the Windows equivalent of the unix side's
# `x copy` (which auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC 52).
#
# Usage:
#   pane-copy.ps1 process [PANE_ID]
#   pane-copy.ps1 coord   [PANE_ID]
#   pane-copy.ps1 content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
#
# Consumers: the prefix+P/D/V/S keybinds and the copy-pane-* herdr-plus Quick
# Actions.

param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)

. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '_common.ps1')

function Show-Usage {
    Write-Host 'usage: pane-copy.ps1 process|coord|content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]'
    exit 64
}

if (-not (Test-HerdrPresent)) { exit 1 }

$argv = @($Argument | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })
if ($argv.Count -lt 1) { Show-Usage }
$action = $argv[0]
$rest = if ($argv.Count -gt 1) { $argv[1..($argv.Count - 1)] } else { @() }

$paneArg = ''
$source = 'recent'
for ($i = 0; $i -lt $rest.Count; $i++) {
    switch -Regex ($rest[$i]) {
        '^--source$' { $source = $rest[++$i] }
        '^--source=' { $source = $rest[$i] -replace '^--source=', '' }
        '^-' { Show-Usage }
        default { if (-not $paneArg) { $paneArg = $rest[$i] } else { Show-Usage } }
    }
}

# herdr-plus passes its own pane var; fall through the same chain otherwise.
if (-not $paneArg -and $env:HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID) { $paneArg = $env:HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID }
$pane = Resolve-HerdrPane -PaneId $paneArg
if (-not $pane) { Show-HerdrNotice 'pane-copy: could not determine a pane id'; exit 1 }

switch ($action) {
    'process' {
        $j = Invoke-HerdrJson pane process-info --pane $pane
        if (-not $j) { Show-HerdrNotice "pane-copy: failed to read process info for $pane"; exit 1 }
        $p = $j.result.process_info
        $lines = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
        $lines.Add("pane $($p.pane_id)  (shell pid $($p.shell_pid))")
        foreach ($fp in @($p.foreground_processes)) {
            if ($fp) { $lines.Add("  $($fp.cmdline)  [pid $($fp.pid), cwd $($fp.cwd)]") }
        }
        if ($lines.Count -eq 1) { $lines.Clear(); $lines.Add("pane $pane  (no foreground processes)") }
        if (Set-HerdrClipboard ($lines -join "`n")) { Write-Host "copied process info for $pane" }
    }
    'coord' {
        $pj = Invoke-HerdrJson pane get $pane
        if (-not $pj) { Show-HerdrNotice "pane-copy: failed to read pane $pane"; exit 1 }
        $ws = $pj.result.pane.workspace_id
        $tb = $pj.result.pane.tab_id
        $pn = $pj.result.pane.pane_id

        $wsj = Invoke-HerdrJson workspace get $ws
        $wsLabel = if ($wsj) { $wsj.result.workspace.label } else { $null }
        $tbj = Invoke-HerdrJson tab get $tb
        $tbLabel = if ($tbj) { $tbj.result.tab.label } else { $null }

        $sock = $env:HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
        $session = 'default'
        if ($sock) {
            $sj = Invoke-HerdrJson session list --json
            if ($sj -and $sj.sessions) {
                $match = $sj.sessions | Where-Object { $_.socket_path -eq $sock } | Select-Object -First 1
                if ($match -and $match.name) { $session = $match.name }
            }
        }

        $lines = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
        $lines.Add("session=$session")
        $lines.Add("workspace=$ws$(if ($wsLabel) { " ($wsLabel)" })")
        $lines.Add("tab=$tb$(if ($tbLabel) { " ($tbLabel)" })")
        $lines.Add("pane=$pn")
        if ($sock) { $lines.Add("socket=$sock") }
        $lines.Add("# herdr pane get $pn")

        if (Set-HerdrClipboard ($lines -join "`n")) { Write-Host "copied coordinate for $pane" }
    }
    'content' {
        if ($source -notin 'visible', 'recent', 'recent-unwrapped') {
            Write-Host 'pane-copy: --source must be visible|recent|recent-unwrapped'
            exit 64
        }
        $body = Get-HerdrPaneText -PaneId $pane -Source $source
        if ($null -eq $body) { Show-HerdrNotice "pane-copy: failed to read content of $pane"; exit 1 }
        if (Set-HerdrClipboard $body) { Write-Host "copied $source content for $pane" }
    }
    default { Show-Usage }
}
```

```ps1
# ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.ps1
# Source: dot_config/herdr/url-pick.ps1 (managed by chezmoi)
#
# herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` (joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). PowerShell port
# of the parent repo's dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh. Reads a herdr
# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), then opens each choice.
#
# The unix version shells out to this repo's `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open);
# the Windows equivalent is Start-Process, which hands the URL to the registered
# shell handler (default browser).
#
# Usage:
#   url-pick.ps1 [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
# --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope); recent scans the
# full retained scrollback.
#
# Consumer: the prefix+u keybind.

param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)

. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '_common.ps1')

function Show-Usage {
    Write-Host 'usage: url-pick.ps1 [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]'
    exit 64
}

if (-not (Test-HerdrPresent)) { exit 1 }
if (-not (Get-Command fzf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Show-HerdrNotice 'url-pick: fzf is required (scoop install fzf)'; exit 1
}

$argv = @($Argument | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })
$paneArg = ''
$source = 'visible'
for ($i = 0; $i -lt $argv.Count; $i++) {
    switch -Regex ($argv[$i]) {
        '^--source$' { $source = $argv[++$i] }
        '^--source=' { $source = $argv[$i] -replace '^--source=', '' }
        '^(-h|--help)$' { Show-Usage }
        '^-' { Show-Usage }
        default { if (-not $paneArg) { $paneArg = $argv[$i] } else { Show-Usage } }
    }
}
if ($source -notin 'visible', 'recent', 'recent-unwrapped') {
    Write-Host 'url-pick: --source must be visible|recent'; exit 64
}

$pane = Resolve-HerdrPane -PaneId $paneArg
if (-not $pane) { Show-HerdrNotice 'url-pick: could not determine a pane id'; exit 1 }

$content = Get-HerdrPaneText -PaneId $pane -Source $source
if ($null -eq $content) { Show-HerdrNotice "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane"; exit 1 }

# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, as .NET regex.
$items = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($content, '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]')) {
    $items.Add($m.Value)
}
foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($content, '(?<!//)\bwww\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*')) {
    $items.Add("http://$($m.Value)")
}
foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($content, '\b[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*')) {
    $items.Add("http://$($m.Value)")
}
# git@host:owner/repo(.git) -> https://host/owner/repo
foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($content, '(ssh://)?git@\S+')) {
    $rewritten = $m.Value -replace '^(ssh://)?git@', '' -replace ':', '/'
    $items.Add("https://$rewritten")
}
foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($content, '[''"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)[''"]')) {
    $items.Add("https://github.com/$($m.Groups[1].Value)")
}
foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($content, 'import\s+[^"'';]*["'']([^.][^"'';]*)["'']')) {
    $items.Add("https://npmjs.com/package/$($m.Groups[1].Value)")
}

$urls = @($items | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)

if ($urls.Count -eq 0) {
    Show-HerdrNotice "url-pick: no URLs found in pane $pane ($source)"
    exit 0
}

# fzf multi-select; Esc / no match -> clean no-op.
$chosen = $urls | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $chosen) { exit 0 }

foreach ($url in @($chosen)) {
    if (-not $url) { continue }
    try { Start-Process $url | Out-Null }
    catch { Write-Host "url-pick: could not open $url ($_)" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
}
```
